title: One slow product blocks the shop
scenario: One slow lamp Inventory call can occupy the shop’s two shared workers. Healthy chair and desk requests then queue or fail, and the whole catalog waits.
why: A short timeout frees workers. A fallback keeps healthy products visible with lamp stock marked as unconfirmed.
reproduce: In Network Faults, add 1500 ms to Inventory. Use “Refresh all availability” and watch shared workers in Grafana.
assignment: Assignment: Can you keep chair and desk available while lamp stock is unconfirmed?

tasks.title: Measure the healthy catalog
tasks.instruction: Refresh all availability. Record stock, catalog time, workers, queue and rejected count. Check “Product p95 latency” and “Shared workers and queue”. Predict the impact and set an abort condition.

tasks.title: Create a lamp-only slowdown
tasks.instruction: Add 1500 ms to Inventory. Keep traffic fixed. Record lamp delay, chair/desk waits or failures, catalog status and new rejections in a fresh window.

tasks.title: Trace the propagation
tasks.instruction: Compare dependency/product p95 latency, workers, queue and rejection rate. Explain how lamp waiting affects healthy products and the catalog.

tasks.title: Apply containment
tasks.instruction: Remove the fault. In Fallbacks & timeouts, apply Challenge 1 settings: 400 ms Inventory timeout plus fallback and breaker. Predict each effect.

tasks.title: Repeat the same fault and verify recovery
tasks.instruction: Repeat the same delay. Compare chair/desk results, queue, new rejections and catalog time, including a 5-second recovery probe. Lamp availability should be disabled while stock is unconfirmed. {{cleanup}}

done: You measured healthy, delayed and mitigated phases under unchanged traffic.
You observed and explained impact on chair/desk or the complete catalog, then verified that impact shrank while lamp stock remained unconfirmed.
You distinguished timeout, circuit breaker and fallback; compared equal windows; and verified cleanup.
solution: Healthy: all products and the catalog return live data quickly. Use your measured timings.
Slow lamp calls occupy shared workers. Healthy products can queue or fail; the catalog waits for every result.
The 400 ms timeout releases workers sooner. The breaker pauses failed lamp calls for 5 seconds; fallback returns unconfirmed stock while chair and desk stay live.
Recovery probes may briefly increase latency. HTTP 200 does not confirm lamp stock. Remove faults, restore defaults and verify recovery.

fields.label: Hypothesis and abort condition
fields.prompt: What will +1500 ms Inventory delay affect? When would you stop?

fields.label: Fault evidence
fields.prompt: Record Inventory latency and customer impact. {{measurementGuidance}}

fields.prompt: Which settings did you use, and why? {{mitigationGuidance}}

fields.prompt: Compare the identical fault after mitigation. {{measurementGuidance}}

fields.prompt: What improved? What remains uncertain? Confirm cleanup.

overview.title: 1 · A slow lamp blocks healthy products
overview.description: Watch shared workers fill, then protect chair and desk with bounded waiting and honest partial results.
